promptState.text: Outpaint the image: replace the solid gray areas with a seamless continuation of the scene, keeping the existing picture unchanged.

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 Load Diffusion Model

Download qwen_image_2.1_int8_convrot.safetensors6.76 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/qwen

Create the qwen folder if it does not exist.

More versions Qwen Image 2.1 model card 

 Load CLIP

Download qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors8.71 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors644 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 LoRA Loader

Download qwen-image-2.1-outpaint-v2.safetensors159 MB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/qwen2.1

Create the qwen2.1 folder if it does not exist.

LoRA model card 

 License: non-commercial use only

Qwen Image 2.1 is released under the Qwen Research License. It allows non-commercial use only, which the license defines as research or evaluation. Commercial use is not included: for that you need a separate license from Qwen.

READ LICENSE 

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Needs ComfyUI 0.37.0 or newer, the first version with the Qwen Image 2.1 nodes. If Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 shows up red, update ComfyUI.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma

How to update Pixaroma nodes: the help page has the steps for every kind of install, in the Update the nodes part.

How to update Pixaroma 

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma - Adds the Outpaint LoRA, right after the model loader. It fills the gray with a continuation of the scene while keeping your picture exactly where it is, which is what lets your original go back in without a seam. It has no trigger word of its own: the first sentence of the prompt is its instruction.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - The picture to extend.
  • 2. Extend the Picture - Outpaint Pixaroma: how much to add, and where. To ratio grows the picture to the shape you pick (here 16:9, so gray is added on both sides of a square picture; the anchor decides which sides). By side adds the number of pixels you type for each edge. The fill is the flat gray #808080 the LoRA was trained on, so leave it as it is. The megapixel limit scales the padded picture to the size the model renders, in steps of 32: 2 MP, the size this LoRA version was trained at.
  • 3. Add a prompt - Keep the first sentence exactly as it is: it is the LoRA's instruction. You can add a description of the picture after it, starting with Scene:.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your picture and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note on the right says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Split Image with Alpha - Qwen Image 2.1 hands back a picture with a transparency channel; this takes the picture part.
  • Outpaint Stitch Pixaroma - Puts your original picture back over the result at full quality and keeps only the new area. feather blends the join over 32 pixels; color match evens out any small colour step along it.
  • Get Image Size - Reads the result's exact size.
  • Upscale Image - Scales the padded picture to that exact size, only for the Compare, so the before and the after line up when you slide between them.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and the padded picture. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes the picture as it comes from step 2. It also makes the blank canvas for the result at that size. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from the LoRA's model card.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - The padded picture with its gray sides and the result, at the same size. Move the mouse across it to slide between them and see what was added.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG, at your picture's own scale.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 720, "height": 1380, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

Your picture made wider: here a square photo of a terrace became 16:9. The model paints the gray sides as a continuation of the scene, more sea and hills on one side and more of the house on the other, and your original goes back in the middle untouched. The demo's 1600 x 1600 picture comes out 2844 x 1600.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 What the LoRA changes

Without the LoRA, Qwen Image 2.1 tends to move or rescale your picture while it fills the gray. Then your original, pasted back by the stitch, no longer lines up with what was painted around it: on the demo the terrace wall stepped at the join and edges showed twice.

Measured on this workflow's demo, the same 8 seeds with the LoRA row on and off, comparing the model's own picture with yours where they overlap: with the LoRA they differed by about 3 brightness levels out of 255 on average, on every seed, which you cannot see; without it by 7 to 44 levels, because the picture had moved.

To see it yourself, switch the LoRA row off, Run the same seed, and look at the joins.

LoRA model card 

 How long a Run takes

Megapixel limitModel rendersNew picture or promptNew seed only
1 MP1344 x 76810 s8 s
2 MP1920 x 105620 s17 s

The limit sets how big the model renders the padded picture. The stitch then scales the new sides up to your picture's own scale, so a bigger limit gives them more detail. Change the picture, the sides or the prompt and the model reads the picture again, which is the first time column; change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second.

 Why the model's picture is a little wider

The megapixel limit rounds each side down to a step of 32 on its own, so the picture the model paints can come out a few percent off your chosen shape. On the demo, 16:9 at 2 MP should be 1930 x 1086; rounded down it is 1920 x 1056, which is 2.3 percent wider. The stitch scales the result back to the exact shape before it puts your original in, so the finished picture is not stretched, and the Resize node does the same for the before picture in the Compare.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 2 MP, it took 17 s, against 22 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out practically the same. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on a 2 MP outpaint: 24 s with the models unloaded first, 17 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 21 GB during these runs, at the 2 MP limit. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

While it renders, the model keeps what it has worked out about your picture and the prompt in a cache, so it does not redo that on every step. The teal node says where that cache lives. Leave it on auto / default: auto keeps the cache in spare graphics memory and moves it to system RAM when that runs out.

On a smaller card, if a run is slow, try dtype int8. It halves the cache, and the node's own description says that can speed things up when memory is short. On this 24 GB card it made no difference (18 s against 17 s at 2 MP). Setting device to cpu, which keeps the cache in system RAM all the time, also cost nothing here (17 s).

 Getting a good extension

  • Extend in steps for a big change. The LoRA's maker found that when your picture is under about 15 percent of the canvas, the model has to invent most of it and the result varies a lot by seed.
  • Words in the new area come out as plausible shapes, not readable text.
  • Leave the gray and the first sentence of the prompt as they are: they are what the LoRA was trained on.
  • Do not add a Set Latent Noise Mask to hold the picture in place: on Qwen 2.1 that draws a visible rectangle at the join, and the LoRA keeps the picture in place by itself.

Tested on 8 seeds: every one continued the hills and the sea on one side and the house on the other, and at full size the joins do not show.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1582, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
